content: Efavirenz and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (DF) both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary when these drugs are used. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, so CYP3A substrates should be monitored if coadministered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. Elivaldogene autotemcel and tenofovir DF reduce each other’s effects. Patients should avoid antiretroviral medications for at least one month before starting stem cell mobilization therapy and during its duration. This applies to elivaldogene autotemcel with lamivudine or doravirine as well. Antiretroviral medications should not be used until all apheresis cycles are completed. Tenofovir DF and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF are contraindicated together. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be combined with other antiretrovirals. Similarly, emtricitabine and lamivudine should not be coadministered due to increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF. Coadministration with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates should be avoided due to potential toxicities. If unavoidable, substrate dosages should be reduced. Encorafenib decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. Encorafenib also increases tenofovir DF levels, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. Enfuvirtide and lamivudine, as well as enfuvirtide and tenofovir DF, increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tenofovir DF increases entecavir levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially increasing toxicity. Both drugs are excreted via active tubular secretion, necessitating caution and monitoring. Enzalutamide decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to potential loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. Lamivudine increases erdafitinib levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and alternatives to OCT2 substrates should be considered, or OCT2 substrate dosages should be reduced. Elicarbazepine acetate decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to potential loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. Tenofovir DF and etodolac increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Toxicity may result from coadministration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Etravirine decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to potential loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. Tenofovir DF increases famciclovir levels by reducing renal clearance, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Fedratinib increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary, and close monitoring is required. Fenofibrate, fenofibrate micronized, and fenofibric acid increase tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance, increasing the risk of myopathy. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tenofovir DF and fenoprofen increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Toxicity may result from coadministration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Fexinidazole increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration should be avoided or alternative drugs used due to increased risk of adverse effects. Flucytosine and tenofovir DF increase each other’s toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Flucytosine increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tenofovir DF and flurbiprofen increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Toxicity may result from coadministration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Fosamprenavir increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is required. Fosamprenavir and lamivudine, as well as fosamprenavir and tenofovir DF, increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Foscarnet and tenofovir DF increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Fosphenytoin decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to potential loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. Fostamatinib increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing metabolism. Coadministration may increase concentrations of BCRP substrate drugs, requiring monitoring for toxicities and potential dosage reductions. Ganciclovir increases tenofovir DF levels, and coadministration with lamivudine increases hematologic toxicity risk. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Gentamicin and tenofovir DF increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Gentamicin increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing elimination. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Givinostat increases lamivudine levels. Givinostat is a weak OAT2 inhibitor, and coadministration with OCT2-sensitive substrates requires close monitoring due to potential toxicities. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing metabolism. Plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates may also increase. Close monitoring is required. Grapefruit increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is required. Tenofovir DF and ibuprofen, including IV ibuprofen, increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Toxicity may result from coadministration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Idelalisib increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is required. Imatinib increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is required. Indinavir increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Indinavir and lamivudine, as well as indinavir and tenofovir DF, increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Tenofovir DF and indomethacin increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Toxicity may result from coadministration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. Interferon alfa-2b and lamivudine increase each other’s toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of liver decompensation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases lamivudine levels. As an OCT2 inhibitor, it may increase the effects or levels of OCT2 substrates. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Isoniazid increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is required. Istradefylline increases tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It also increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required, and dose reductions of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. Itraconazole increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration may increase doravirine plasma concentrations and toxicities. Close monitoring is required. Ivosidenib decreases doravirine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to potential loss of virologic response and resistance to doravirine. Ketoconazole increases doravirine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Tenofovir DF and ketoprofen increase each other’s levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Toxicity may result from coadministration with drugs excreted via glomerular filtration or active tubular secretion, including high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered.
